note: THE ONE LAW, WRITTEN ONCE (pds-w28-bl-two-rerun-screens-drift). Wave 28 landed two hand-maintained screens for 'which rerun spellings are legal': the Elixir WRITE seam (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/stage.ex @forbidden_rerun_shapes, reachable as Barkpark.Tasks.Stage.rerun_refusal_code/1) and the JS READ seam (tooling/pds/spellings.mjs forbiddenSpelling). Neither re-derived that it agreed with the other, and three measured spellings already disagreed. It lives under api/test/fixtures/ rather than tooling/pds/fixtures/ because scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh forbids the Elixir suite from reading a repo-root path elixir.yml does not dispatch on: a fixture under tooling/pds/** would be read by an Elixir suite CI never re-runs when the fixture changes. The JS gate reaches into api/ for it instead. This file is the mirror lock: BOTH suites read THIS file and assert their own column against it. It is never two retyped copies. A spelling that is not listed here is not screened by anything that would notice a widening.
loader_contract: Both loaders MUST refuse an empty or unparseable read (zero cases) rather than pass vacuously. A lock that can go quiet is not a lock. Elixir: api/test/barkpark/tasks/rerun_spelling_mirror_test.exs. JS: tooling/pds/rerun-adjudicate.test.mjs section 3b.

precedence.why: A fixture that pins only the VALUE SET is blind to an arm ORDER swapped on one side: a command can breach two rules, and the screen reports the FIRST match, which is the one the author has to fix first. Wave 28 shipped the two screens with arms 2 and 4 transposed — `test -f x && git merge-base --is-ancestor a b` was :merge_base_ancestor to the writer and TEST-F to the reader. So the order is pinned too, and multi_breach cases below only pass while both orders hold.

class_map_note: pipe_masked maps to PIPE-MASKED-RC, which is NOT a spellings.mjs rule name — it is variance.mjs's over-claim label. The mismatch is deliberate and is exactly what forces the divergence sentence on that case: the two seams handle pipe masking at DIFFERENT layers, and the lock must not be able to call that agreement.
agreement_rule: For every case: class_map[case.elixir] must equal case.js, OR case.divergence must be a non-empty sentence saying why the two seams are deliberately different there. Both suites assert this, so an undocumented widening of either screen reds.

cases.why: THE ORDER CASE. Two rules fire; the first-listed wins. Wave 28 shipped the arms transposed — writer said :merge_base_ancestor, reader said TEST-F — so a set-only fixture would have called this pair identical. The READER's RULES array was reordered to the writer's order.
the redirect is arm 1 on both sides and outranks the ancestry rule; pins the top of the order

cases.divergence: INTENDED, AND RECORDED RATHER THAN CLOSED. The write seam refuses a formatting pipeline tail as a fifth shape (check_rerun_pipe_tail/1) because a stored rerun that cannot fail is worthless at write time. The read seam deliberately does NOT refuse it at the SPELLING layer: tooling/pds/variance.mjs already grades it one layer over as the PIPE-MASKED-RC over-claim, which demotes the claim instead of discarding the row, and that is a more informative answer for an already-stored command. Adding a fifth RULE here would double-screen it and change adjudication output. The direction is safe: the writer is stricter, so the failure mode is a false REFUSAL at write time, never a false accept.
cases.why: `git show origin/main:<gone>` exits 128; the same command piped to `head -1` exits 0 — the formatter launders the failure into a pass
